Document title: Learning optimal solutions for extremely fast AC optimal power flow : preprint /
Document description: The document discusses a machine learning approach to optimize the real-time operation of electric grids. The authors aim to learn feasible solutions to the AC optimal power flow problem with negligible optimality gaps. They propose a two-stage learning-based AC OPF solver that uses efficient modeling of the AC OPF solutions and feasibility recovering stage. The approach eliminates the need to directly tackle the AC OPF optimization problem, use approximations, linearizations, or convexifications of the power flow equations, and use distributed techniques or computationally intensive platforms. The authors use a novel parameterization of the AC OPF solutions to enforce generation limits and strictly feasible solutions to train the learning model. The output of the model is constrained to adhere to active power generation and voltage magnitude constraints. The goal of the proposed data-driven approach is to learn the underlying OPF mapping between the load demand at all load buses and the generators' active power and voltage magnitude set points. The authors aim to determine generation set points on timescales that are appropriate for balancing fast fluctuations in renewable generation and load. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly decrease the computational burden for grid operators and provide near-optimal and feasible AC OPF solutions.

Document description: CINELDI was an eight-year research centre focused on developing environment-friendly energy solutions to modernize electricity distribution grids. Over the eight years, the centre published approximately 250 scientific articles and developed Norwegian reference grids for grid companies and researchers. Key research themes included digitalization and flexible utilization of the power grid, with a strong emphasis on open access to data and code while protecting sensitive information. Additionally, 150 students completed their master's theses under the centre's guidance, and research scientists helped develop new study programs in electrification and digitalization. The centre facilitated collaboration between technology providers, grid companies, and scientists to drive innovation and standardization in the industry. Through pilot projects, the centre generated 50 innovations that improved work processes and decision-making support for grid operators. The results from CINELDI laid the groundwork for the subsequent SecurEL centre, which focuses on security of electricity supply and continues the work towards a robust energy future.

Document description: Digital solutions hold great potential to accelerate the transformation of power systems to contribute to energy security, affordability, sustainability, and reliability, and thereby support the global community on its pathway to prosperity for everyone. It also recommends that the G7 and international community unlock system value through tailored digitalisation strategies, accelerate digital orchestration through system-wide co-ordination, and rethink skills and training to integrate education topics and digital literacy.

Document title: Model-free primal-dual methods for network optimization with application to real-time optimal power flow : preprint /
Document description: This paper examines the problem of real-time optimization of networked systems and develops online algorithms that steer the system towards the optimal trajectory without explicit knowledge of the system model. The problem is modeled as a dynamic optimization problem with time-varying performance objectives and engineering constraints. The design of the algorithms leverages the online zero-order primal-dual projected-gradient method, replacing the primal step that involves the gradient of the objective function with its zero-order approximation using a deterministic perturbation signal. The evaluations are performed using the measurements of the system output, giving rise to a feedback interconnection, with the optimization algorithm serving as a feedback controller. The paper provides some insights on the stability and tracking properties of this interconnection. Finally, the paper applies this methodology to a real-time optimal power flow problem in power systems, and shows its efficacy on the IEEE 37-node distribution test feeder for reference power tracking and voltage regulation.

Document title: The use of AI for improving energy security
Document description: The document discusses the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) applications to improve energy security in the European power grid. It highlights the challenges facing the grid, including aging infrastructure, rising demand, and the need to decarbonize energy supplies. The authors propose that AI applications can address these challenges by increasing energy security through demand response, improving wind farm efficiency, and facilitating the integration of electric vehicles into the grid. However, they also note that the widespread deployment of AI applications could come with cybersecurity risks, supplier dependency, and vendor lock-in. The document presents a technical report that accompanies a main policy report, describing the methods, tools, and results of a quantitative exploration of the impact of AI-based applications on the energy security of the European power grid. The authors evaluate the impact of three AI applications across four scenarios, finding that AI-driven load reduction provided benefits across all energy security metrics, while AI-driven load shifting improved two metrics but left the others unchanged. The distributional impact varied between countries, with some showing improvement and others remaining unchanged or deteriorating. The document concludes that the impact of AI on energy security will depend on how it is rolled out, and that trade-offs between countries and different metrics are possible.

Document title: Optimal power flow methods and their application to distribution systems with energy storage : a survey of available tools and methods
Document description: This report surveys the available methods and tools for solving optimal power flow (OPF) problems, with a focus on the application of energy storage in distribution systems. The OPF problem is a large class of optimization problems for power system applications, where one requires that any solutions respect the power flow equations for the system. The purpose of solving OPF problems is to optimize the operation or planning of a power system according to a defined criterion while meeting all system constraints, including the power flow constraints. The report discusses various methods available in the scientific literature and implemented in software tools, including gradient methods, Newton-based methods, sequential approximation algorithms, and interior-point methods. It also presents a survey of available software tools implementing OPF methods, including commercial software tools such as PSS, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, and PowerWorld Simulator. The report aims to provide a better overview of what software tools are available for performing optimal power flow analyses and to create the basis for developing new research activities and projects on topics related to the optimization of distribution systems with energy storage.

Document title: DC Grid Integration: Literature Review and Technical Focus
Document description: The Dutch electricity system faces severe congestion due to rapid electrification and renewable energy deployment, creating a mismatch with existing alternating current infrastructure as the grid transitions toward converter-dominated operation. This document reviews literature and technical aspects of direct current microgrids and hybrid architectures to address these challenges by improving efficiency, flexibility, and grid utilization. Direct current microgrids offer structural advantages by eliminating reactive power and phase-angle constraints, which allows for more direct and controllable power flows within distribution networks. Reducing multiple conversion stages in these systems decreases losses and local peak loading, thereby enhancing the overall hosting capacity for renewable energy. However, the lack of inherent inertia in direct current systems leads to fast voltage dynamics that require advanced control strategies to maintain stability. Coordinated hierarchical control frameworks are essential to manage these dynamics, relying heavily on communication reliability and coordination between distributed converters and energy storage systems. Protection strategies for direct current systems are also more complex due to rapid fault propagation and the absence of natural current zero-crossings. The report integrates surveys of European research projects and Dutch demonstrators to connect theoretical developments with real-world implementation experiences. While these initiatives prove the technical feasibility of direct current and hybrid systems in applications like EV charging hubs and smart buildings, they also reveal limitations in fully integrated system operation. The document identifies key research gaps and proposes a methodological framework to guide future work by combining congestion-aware operation with coordinated control and protection strategies. This framework aims to assess the viability and scalability of direct current architectures while providing actionable guidelines for distribution system operators and policymakers.

Document title: Robust matrix completion state estimation in distribution systems : preprint /
Document description: This document presents a robust matrix completion state estimation method for distribution systems. The method combines matrix completion and power system models to estimate voltage in a low-observability condition. It improves the robustness of the matrix completion state estimation to bad data by minimizing the rank of the matrix and measurements residual with different weights. The proposed method is formulated as a convex optimization problem and solved by a semidefinite programming solver. It is numerically evaluated on the IEEE 33-node radial distribution system and compared with the weighted least squares and matrix completion state estimation methods. The results show that the proposed method has better estimation performance and robustness to bad data. The method can estimate the system state in a low-observability system without the bad data detection process. It has the potential to be used in real-time monitoring and analysis in distribution systems.

Document title: The application of AI and big data in power systems
Document description: The electricity grid is undergoing a profound transformation due to the integration of renewable energy, power electronics, and flexible loads, which creates complex operational challenges requiring high-frequency sensing and dynamic decision-making. Conventional methods relying on static models are becoming inadequate, necessitating the application of artificial intelligence and big data technologies to achieve datadriven operations and model-guided optimization. This report outlines how the integration of these technologies enables closed-loop mechanisms that encompass perception, cognition, decision, and control through the use of machine learning, deep neural networks, and knowledge graphs. The findings indicate that AI is evolving from localized technical support to a systemic capability, demonstrating significant value in areas such as power forecasting, dispatch optimization, and risk assessment. While the synergistic development of intelligent algorithms and digital twins empowers power systems with capabilities for self-learning and self-recovery, the large-scale application still faces challenges like fragmented data resources and insufficient algorithm interpretability. The report emphasizes the need to establish a closed-loop system covering data, models, computing power, and governance to ensure the safe, trustworthy, and sustainable application of AI in power systems. Future developments are expected to lead the intelligent and low-carbon transformation of power systems through technological innovation and policy coordination, resulting in higher levels of security and flexibility.

Overall, the study aims to develop informed growth plans that balance network capacity with cost optimization strategies.

Document title: Enhancement of distribution system state estimation using pruned physics-aware neural networks : preprint /
Document description: The document discusses the enhancement of distribution system state estimation using pruned physics-aware neural networks. The authors propose a new method called the pruned physics-aware neural network (P2N2) to improve voltage estimation accuracy in the distribution system. The method relies on the physical grid topology to design the connections between different hidden layers of a neural network model. The authors use a numerical simulation based on one-year smart meter data to generate measurement and voltage state data. The IEEE 123-node system is selected as the test network to benchmark the proposed algorithm against the classic weighted least squares (WLS). The results show that P2N2 outperforms WLS in terms of data redundancy and estimation accuracy. The authors also discuss the challenges of realizing complete observability in the three-phase distribution system and propose a data-driven state estimation with limited sensing to solve the problem.

Document title: The use of AI for improving energy security
Document description: Modern civilisation is critically dependent on access to electricity. Electricity systems underpin practically all the essential life functions we take for granted. However, existing grid systems were not designed to handle present – let alone future – electricity demand. Climate change urgently demands drastic changes to our energy systems. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications have potential to solve many of the challenges facing the grid. They can fulfil a range of functions throughout the electricity system, making electricity cheaper and more reliable. However, the deployment of AI applications could also give rise to cybersecurity risks, the risk of unexplained or unexpected actions, or supplier dependency and vendor lock-in. The speed at which AI is developing means many of these risks are not yet well understood. This report provides an overview of state-of-the-art AI deployment in the electricity system and discusses the risks and opportunities AI tools may bring for electricity systems.

Document title: Primod – A fundamental short-term model for power system analyses and multimarket price forecasting
Document description: The document describes a short-term hydrothermal scheduling model named Primod, developed within the research project 'Pricing Balancing Services in the Future Nordic Power Market'. Primod is based on linear programming and mixed integer linear programming for solving the unit commitment and least cost dispatch problem for a short-time horizon. The model comprises co-optimization of electricity and reserve capacity and a separate module for studying the costs and marginal costs of handling system imbalances. The Nordic power market is in transition, with a need for long-term forecasts of prices and operational costs associated with all electricity products. Fundamental market models have and will play an important role in providing consistent forecasts of power system costs and prices. The Primod model is primarily intended for analyses of the hydro-dominated Nordic power market. The model is part of a toolchain, which includes a long-term model and a mid-term model, to capture the effects of more short-term variations in both demand and production. The toolchain is developed and maintained by SINTEF Energy Research.

Document description: This document discusses the use of a curriculum learned controller to restore critical loads in resilient distribution systems. The curriculum is designed to guide the reinforcement learning agent to escape poorly-performing local optima and learn a better control policy. The document highlights the potential benefits of using reinforcement learning for critical load restoration, including faster and more accurate control, and the ability to directly learn from a nonlinear unbalanced multi-phase AC power flow model. Document description: State estimation is a mathematical method used for determining the most-likely current behavior of a power grid based on a set of measurements and the structure of the network itself. This method has been used on transmission systems for decades to achieve and calibrate network visibility, but it is not yet widely adopted for distribution system operations outside demonstration areas. The report concludes an investigation by Smarter Grid Solutions into the application of state estimation for distribution systems, evaluating initiatives supporting development, use cases, implementation challenges, state-of-the-art literature, gaps in literature and demonstration projects, and best practices for state estimation. The report also provides a software toolkit with which some state estimation concepts may be explored in a hands-on experiential environment. Research into state estimation has gone on for two decades, but there exists a real gap between academic understanding and operational practices. Many of the implementation challenges have their root in the fundamental differences between transmission and distribution systems. The report provides the material necessary to understand the context and workings of state estimation, as well as offers practical information on how to evaluate a plan for implementing an estimator.

Document title: Utility Perspectives on Making Grid-Enhancing Technologies Work
Document description: The U.S. electricity transmission grid faces significant challenges including rising demand, a changing resource mix, and an aging infrastructure that requires transformative solutions. While long-term transmission expansion is essential for reliability, the lengthy permitting and construction processes necessitate immediate, flexible alternatives. Grid-enhancing technologies offer a viable near-term strategy to improve system performance by unlocking capacity and reducing congestion without new rights-of-way. These technologies include dynamic line rating, advanced conductors, advanced power flow control, and transmission topology optimization, which can be deployed in months rather than years. Real-world examples demonstrate their effectiveness, such as PPL Electric's line rating increase and Southern California Edison's conductor installations. Despite these benefits, barriers such as modeling uncertainties, regulatory ambiguity, and organizational resistance remain. The report synthesizes utility experiences and recommendations to accelerate the adoption of these technologies into standard practice. By integrating these tools with long-term planning, stakeholders can create a more resilient and efficient grid capable of meeting future demands.

Document title: ESIF 2019
Document description: The document discusses the Energy Systems Integration Facility (ESIF) and its role in developing and evaluating energy systems. The ESIF has grown exponentially in importance since its creation six years ago and is now a meeting ground for partners to explore energy concepts. The facility is looking to the future, focusing on resilience and security, integrated modeling and simulation, and studies at an even greater scale. The National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) has welcomed a new research asset, the Eagle supercomputer, which will support innovation and demonstrate it. The ESIF will also be a critical component of the Advanced Research for Integrated Energy Systems (ARIES) initiative, which will expand capabilities at both the ESIF and NREL's Flatirons Campus. The document also discusses the Grid Modernization Initiative (GMI) and its focus on developing a coordinated approach to grid modernization research across the national laboratories. The GMI is a crosscutting effort that focuses public and private partnerships to develop a portfolio of new tools and technologies that measure, analyze, predict, protect, and control the grid of the future. The GMI has expanded its vision to include more participation across the Department of Energy, a focus on fully integrated energy systems, and increased security and resilience. The initiative is implementing this vision by investing approximately $80 million through its latest lab call. NREL supports the GMI through the Grid Modernization Laboratory Consortium (GMLC), a strategic partnership between the Department of Energy and the national laboratories that brings together leading experts, technologies, and resources to modernize the nation's electric grid.

Document title: The Internet of Things in the Power Sector: Opportunities in Asia and the Pacific
Document description: The Internet of Things (IoT) has the potential to significantly transform the industrial sector. IoT solutions are entering the domain of industrial operations in the power sector, with applications such as condition monitoring and predictive maintenance of assets. In Asia, many grids are plagued with unreliable service due to aging equipment, poor maintenance, and high demand growth rates. Investment in IoT can reduce unscheduled downtime, improve reliability, and reduce costs. IoT can also be used to optimize the use of generation assets, increase efficiency of production, and reduce emissions. A futuristic application of IoT is a holistic optimization of the entire power network, achieving decentralization and defossilization of the power sector. Several challenges to the adoption of IoT in Asia and the Pacific include financial constraints, investment requirements, and the need for new infrastructure. The Asian Development Bank has a unique position to enable IoT transformation through results-based lending and other financial vehicles. IoT investment should be done alongside new infrastructure investments. In Asia, several pilots of smart meters, smart buildings, and smart cities are ongoing, with potential benefits including improved customer service, reduced costs, and increased energy access.

Document title: SPS4SE System Integrity Protection Schemes for added transfer capacity : Final Project Report
Document description: This document is the final project report for the Swedish research project 'System Integrity Protection Schemes for added transfer capacity' (SPS4SE), which aimed to increase knowledge about System Integrity Protection Schemes as part of the smart transmission grid to enable reliable and secure capacity increases in existing Swedish and Nordic power systems. The report defines SIPS as automatic systems that apply curative control actions in response to critical conditions to increase power system reliability and available capacity, distinguishing them from preventive measures. The project investigated the current Nordic deployment of SIPS, finding significant variation between countries from under ten schemes in Finland to over 300 in Norway, with common uses including protection from component overload and management of converter-interactions related to wind power integration. Two doctoral research projects were conducted, one at Lund University focusing on flow-based capacity calculation methods and voltage stability constrained systems, and another at the Royal Institute of Technology focusing on data-driven decision support using machine learning for transient instability assessment and reinforcement learning for topological remedial actions. The report also presents international examples of emerging SIPS solutions from Australia, Spain, France and Sweden, and concludes with recommendations for future development including advanced visualization techniques and enhanced computer-based schemes to manage increasingly complex power systems.

Document description: This document presents a federated architecture for secure and transactive distributed energy resource management solutions, known as FAST-DERMS. The system aims to provide reliable, resilient, and secure transmission and distribution grid services through the scalable aggregation and near-real-time management of utility-scale and small-scale distributed energy resources. The architecture relies on several key components, including distributed energy resources, flexible resource schedulers, coordinators, aggregators, and transactive market managers. The system follows a 'total DSO' approach to enable interactions between distributed energy resources at distribution networks and transmission system operators. FAST-DERMS provides a scalable and interoperable approach for distribution utilities to aggregate and control various distributed energy resources to participate in wholesale electricity markets and provide transmission grid services. The system also incorporates approaches to detect anomalies and provide a fail-safe to secure grid operations in the presence of cyber-physical attacks.

Document title: Quantum technologies: Can they boost Europe's decarbonisation?
Document description: This briefing examines the potential of quantum technologies to accelerate the European Union's decarbonisation efforts and support its climate neutrality goals by 2050. While quantum computing, sensing, and communication offer transformative capabilities for sectors like heavy industry and energy grids, their specific role in decarbonisation has historically received fragmented policy attention. The document outlines how quantum applications could revolutionise the design of green hydrogen catalysts, improve battery efficiency, and enhance carbon capture technologies through advanced simulations. Currently, the EU supports these technologies through initiatives such as the Quantum Flagship and Horizon Europe, yet there is a lack of a coordinated strategy explicitly linking quantum research to climate objectives. With the expected adoption of a quantum act in 2026, policymakers are urged to integrate long-term decarbonisation targets into the research framework to leverage scientific leadership. The briefing also reviews global initiatives from countries like the UK, US, Australia, and China, highlighting varying approaches to funding and application focus. Despite significant investments and promising applications, the EU faces challenges in translating innovation into market opportunities and achieving critical mass across member states. Ultimately, the document suggests that quantum technologies should be viewed as accelerators for clean energy innovation rather than primary solutions, requiring strategic alignment to bridge the innovation gap for net-zero emissions.

Document description: This report examines the technical opportunities and challenges associated with integrating capacity expansion models for electricity system planning to address factors like load growth and decarbonization. The report emphasizes that optimizing distributed energy resources requires specific data development and alignment with existing utility valuation mechanisms. Ultimately, it proposes a step-by-step approach for planners to move from basic iterative improvements toward more comprehensive, optimized planning outcomes.

Document title: Rapid QSTS Simulations for High-Resolution Comprehensive Assessment of Distributed PV
Document description: The document discusses the need for comprehensive interconnection modeling and impact analysis of distributed energy resources on the electric power distribution system. Quasi-static time-series (QSTS) simulations are used to model time-dependent voltage controllers and the diversity of potential impacts that can occur at different times of year. However, these simulations can be computationally burdensome, taking 10 to 120 hours to complete for a year-long simulation at 1-second resolution. To address this issue, the authors developed accurate and computationally efficient QSTS methods that can be implemented in existing open-source and commercial software. These methods include variable time-step, vector quantization, event-based, intelligent sample selection, machine learning, diakoptics, temporal parallelization, and circuit reduction. The authors also developed methods to create high-resolution proxy data sets. The target performance level for this project was achieved with year-long high-resolution time series solutions run in less than 5 minutes within an acceptable error.

The report highlights the laboratory's high-performance computing (HPC) capabilities, including the development of a new supercomputer named Kestrel, which will accelerate energy efficiency and renewable energy research at a pace and scale more than five times greater than the current supercomputer. NREL continues to push the boundaries of efficient data center operation, with warm water cooling, optimization, and waste heat recovery enabling the facility to end the year with an average power usage effectiveness rating of 1.031. The report also mentions the ESIF Insight Center, which provides advanced visualization technology to promote knowledge discovery in energy systems. Additionally, the report discusses the development of a visual analytics capability that takes full advantage of the Insight Center's new 100-million-pixel display. Researchers at NREL see an urgent alarm in the convergence of known and unknown biases in artificial intelligence and are working to quantify how bias gets introduced in modeling, simulation, and other scientific or analytic processes.

Document title: SPS4SE System Integrity Protection Schemes for added transfer capacity : Final Project Report
Document description: The SPS4SE project aims to increase knowledge on System Integrity Protection Schemes (SIPS) and their application in the Swedish power grid and the Nordic power system. SIPS are automatic systems that apply curative control actions to protect the system integrity and increase available capacity. The project has resulted in several scientific publications and collaboration activities. Research has focused on flow-based capacity calculation methods, voltage stability constrained systems, and data-driven decision support for SIPS. The study has shown that SIPS can increase trading capacities and monetary value, and that they can be used to manage new phenomena such as converter-interactions related to wind-power integration. The project has also investigated the use of SIPS in the Nordic power system, including the current situation of SIPS deployment and use. The study has shown that SIPS are used in different ways in different countries, and that they can be used to enable increased grid utilization and to manage new phenomena. The project has also proposed new SIPS solutions and investigated their potential applications. The study has shown that SIPS can be used to provide increased support to operators, such as advanced visualization techniques. The project has also discussed the dual objectives of SIPS, which are to provide a defence in case of extreme events and to enable increased grid capacity. The study has shown that SIPS can enable faster integration of renewable generation and provide enhanced security of electric power supply. The project has received funding from the Swedish Energy Agency and has been supported by expertise from Nordic transmission system operators and industry representatives.

Document title: HPC at NREL: FY 2019
Document description: The document discusses the high-performance computing (HPC) capabilities at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). NREL's HPC User Facility supports 182 modeling and simulation projects advancing the mission across the spectrum of energy efficiency and renewable energy technologies. The new HPC system, Eagle, was delivered in September 2018 and put into production on January 2, 2019, replacing the previous system Peregrine. Eagle has a peak performance of 8 petaflops and is the world's largest supercomputer dedicated to energy efficiency and renewable energy. The system is used for various projects, including the simulation of ion transport in disordered multinary chalcogenides, the evaluation of energy retrofit scenarios for residential buildings, and the determination of the detailed dissociation mechanism for the cellulose-degrading enzyme TrCel7A. The document also highlights the energy efficiency of NREL's ESIF HPC Data Center, which has achieved a world-leading annualized average power usage effectiveness (PUE) rating of 1.036. The data center uses best-in-class technologies and has implemented a prototype carbon-free data center concept based on automotive-scale hydrogen fuel cells. The document also describes the various data analysis and visualization capabilities available at NREL, including the Insight Center and the Apache Spark module for the Eagle HPC system.

Document title: IEA Wind TCP: Results of IEA Wind TCP Workshop on a Grand Vision for Wind Energy Technology
Document description: The wind industry has experienced significant growth, with over 500 gigawatts of installed capacity in 2017 and producing about 5% of global electricity demand in 2016. The levelized cost of energy for wind energy projects has decreased due to innovation, making it competitive with natural gas fuel and solar electricity generation. However, there are challenges facing continued growth, including competition from solar photovoltaics and shale gas, as well as concerns about the ability to maintain a reliable and stable electric grid system operation as wind-generated electricity increases. To realize the full potential of wind technology, a paradigm shift is required in how wind turbines and power plants are designed, controlled, and operated. The IEA Wind Topical Experts Meeting (TEM) #89 'Grand Vision for Wind Energy' workshop brought together experts to consider how to enable a future in which wind energy supplies more than 50% of global electricity consumption. The workshop identified key R&D challenges and innovation pathways to reduce the levelized cost of energy and increase the system value of wind energy. The report highlights the need for overarching coordination efforts and frameworks to address the R&D challenges and realize the Grand Vision for wind energy.

Document title: SPS4SE System Integrity Protection Schemes for added transfer capacity : Final Project Report
Document description: The document discusses the findings and final results from the Swedish research project 'System Integrity Protection Schemes for added transfer capacity' (SPS4SE). The project aimed to increase knowledge on System Integrity Protection Schemes (SIPS) and their utilization to support a sustainable development of the Swedish power grid and the Nordic power system. SIPS are automatic systems that apply curative control actions to increase power system reliability and/or available capacity. The project involved two PhD projects, one at Lunds University Faculty of Engineering (LTH) and one at the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH), which focused on flow-based capacity calculation methods, voltage stability constrained systems, and data-driven decision support related to SIPS. The research showed that SIPS can provide significant societal gains, enabling faster integration of renewable generation and enhanced security of electric power supply. The project also highlighted the need for a Swedish standard for SIPS terminology and proposed novel emergency power control strategies for VSC-HVDC links. The results of the project have been presented in several scientific publications and other collaboration and outreach activities.

Document title: ARIES Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems Research Plan
Document description: The energy system is undergoing a transformation, driven by the increasing adoption of renewable energy sources, electric vehicles, and smart energy management systems. This transformation requires a new national capability to conduct integrated research at the interface between distribution and bulk power systems. The Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems (ARIES) platform aims to address the challenges of integrated energy systems at scale, including managing variability in new energy technologies, controlling large numbers of interconnected devices, and integrating multiple diverse technologies. ARIES will explore new connections among ever-changing technologies and overlapping energy domains, ensuring that the nation's energy system remains secure, stable, efficient, and effective at all scales. The research objectives of ARIES are framed around the integration needs and opportunities of increased penetrations of low-cost variable generation and storage, increased power electronics-based management and controls, and the need for advanced sensing and data analytics. The ARIES platform will create an environment to address these challenges and advance future innovations in energy systems.

Document title: Transport-technology research innovation grants (T-TRIG): project reviews
Document description: The document discusses the Transport-Technology Research and Innovation Grants (T-TRIG) programme, which was launched in 2014 by the Department for Transport. The programme aims to foster innovation in the transport sector, generate growth, and build links between policy teams and innovators. The 2019 cohort of T-TRIG projects demonstrated the depth of ingenuity and breadth of imagination of UK innovators, featuring a highly diverse spread of projects covering all transport modes. The programme has made 199 grant offers since 2014, investing around £6m in innovation support primarily to SMEs and start-ups. The 2019 call provided £900k to fund 30 six-month projects across four themes: decarbonising the transport system, open call, age-friendly and accessible transport, and potholes and resilient infrastructure. The programme has had a significant impact, with successful businesses developing and thriving since their involvement with T-TRIG. The programme has also led to its mechanisms being adopted across the Department for Transport and by other government departments.

Document title: Photovoltaic and Behind-the-Meter Battery Storage: Advanced Smart Inverter Controls and Field Demonstration
Document description: The document discusses a project by the California Energy Commission's Energy Research and Development Division to develop and demonstrate advanced smart inverter controls for photovoltaic and behind-the-meter battery storage systems. The project aimed to create a centralized resource to test and validate distribution technology controls with industry-standard PV, storage, and high-fidelity sensors. It also sought to promote new ways to control clusters of PV smart inverters, innovate, develop, and field-test a predictive controller to maximize profit for the customer while supporting the grid. The controller was built using state-of-the-art model predictive control methodology to optimally control behind-the-meter PV and battery storage. The project evaluated the potential cost-effectiveness of behind-the-meter battery storage and found that it could save as much as 35 percent of an annual electricity bill, with a payback of the investment in battery storage in about 6 years. The developed simulation models, grid event library, and model predictive controller are open-source and available online.

Document description: This interim report from the International Telecommunication Union's Telecommunication Standardization Bureau details the progress of the Innovate for Impact project, which aims to identify and support practical artificial intelligence solutions that create tangible benefits for people and communities. Launched in 2024, the initiative expanded its scope in 2025 through an open call that received 234 submissions from 32 countries, with 160 selected for inclusion in this document. To ensure high-quality evaluation, the project established a Technical Advisory Committee comprising thirty-two experts and selected sixteen AI scholars to assist in analyzing and refining the submitted solutions. The report highlights eleven key domains where these applications are being deployed, covering areas such as healthcare, education, climate resilience, and digital inclusion. It presents a comprehensive view of concepts, practical implementations, and lessons learned from global use cases while emphasizing the importance of responsible AI deployment. The document also acknowledges support from China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and outlines a pathway for future work to deepen collaboration with partners worldwide. Ultimately, the report serves as a resource for sharing expertise and accelerating the deployment of inclusive and impactful artificial intelligence solutions across various sectors.

Document title: Design Optimal Feedback Control Using Evolutionary Particle Swarm Optimization in Multi- Machine Power System
Document description: This document discusses the application of Evolutionary Particle Swarm Optimization (EPSO) to design weighting matrices Q and R elements in Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) optimization process. The authors propose using EPSO to determine the elements of matrices Q and R, which are crucial components in the LQR optimization method. The proposed method considers two kinds of loads: static and dynamic loads. The static load illustrates a load characteristic as a momentary function of magnitude voltage and frequency, while the dynamic load describes active power and reactive power as a function of voltage and frequency magnitude at past and present instant times. The authors compare the results of using EPSO and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to determine the elements of matrices Q and R. The proposed method is expected to produce the optimal feedback control gain K for large power systems. The authors also discuss the design of Centralized Optimal Feedback Control (COFC) for a multi-machine power system model. The COFC design is demonstrated using seven generators, twenty buses, and 500 kV transmission lines. The authors conclude that the proposed method is effective in determining the elements of matrices Q and R, which are crucial for the optimal feedback control of large power systems.

Document description: The African Development Bank Group has launched the Africa Infrastructure Knowledge Program to improve the availability of statistical information on infrastructure development on the continent. The program aims to provide an effective and sustainable platform for data collection and analysis on Africa's infrastructure sectors, including electricity, transport, ICT, and water and sanitation. The report 'Estimating Investment Needs for the Power Sector in Africa 2023-2030' provides a comprehensive analysis of the financial investments required to bridge the energy gap in Africa. The study estimates that a base case investment requirement of about USD 454 billion, or USD 64 billion per year from 2023 until 2030, is needed to achieve universal access to electricity in Africa. The report also highlights the urgent need for concerted action and the profound impact that strategic investments can have on the continent's future. The study aims to derive insights from economic least-cost expansion modelling to estimate economic least-cost investment requirements and related emissions, and to explore existing structural barriers to and enablers of the energy transition. The report sheds light on the uncertainties inherent to modelling exercises of this nature, but also provides several interesting insights. The scenario analyses prepared for this study indicate that moving the goalpost for universal access to 2040 would reduce the number of connections required till 2030 by 70 million, or 36 percent. The largest reduction in absolute numbers would be seen in Western and Eastern Africa. Overall, the number of off-grid connections needed across Africa until 2030 is nearly halved in the Delayed Access Scenario. The economic least-cost and low-emissions power system expansion pathways for Africa towards 2030 are largely the same. It is forecasted that total net energy demand on the African continent will grow by 44 percent to around 1,200 TWh between 2023 and 2030. While Southern and Northern Africa will see the largest absolute growth, the highest relative increase is expected in Central and Eastern Africa as a result of access expansion. The core of the power system expansion analysis in this Study entails optimization of power supply options and interconnection for each country by minimizing system costs to meet the forecasted demand hour-by-hour through the year in realistic wind, solar irradiation, and hydrological conditions. The Base Case results reconfirm the cost-competitiveness of variable renewables, predominantly wind and solar across the Continent. This is true even when accounting for necessary co-investments in spinning and non-spinning reserves, batteries, and interconnectors required to offset the challenges that variable generation pose to power grids. In total, the least-cost Base Case requires a net expansion of generation capacity of 182 GW from 2023 until 2030, 88 percent of which would come from variable renewables such as wind and solar.

Document title: Decentralized Economic Dispatch for Radial Electric Distribution Systems
Document description: The document discusses the importance of decentralizing economic dispatch for radial electric distribution systems. It presents a thesis that introduces an alternative algorithm for dispatching power while accounting for heterogeneous demand functions across customers. The algorithm is computationally feasible, respects the physical limits of the system, and converges to the same solution as a centralized operator with perfect information. The thesis also explores the potential benefits of a distribution system operator, including resiliency, encouraging the integration of distributed energy resources, reliability, and reducing transportation losses. The document also touches on the topic of energy transactions at the distribution level, including the role of a distribution system operator and the potential for energy trading platforms. The author presents a proof-of-concept example on a 46-bus system and estimates the economic implications of energy transactions.

Document title: Research and innovation for a secure, resilient and sustainable electricity grid – FME SecurEL : position paper (CINELDI report 01:2025)
Document description: The document describes the research and innovation needs for developing a secure, resilient and sustainable electricity grid for the future. FME SecurEL is a Norwegian centre for environment-friendly energy research that aims to enable the transition to a net-zero emissions society by developing sustainable electricity distribution grids. The centre will focus on safeguarding the security of electricity supply by maximising grid utilisation in a secure, resilient, and sustainable way. SecurEL has two main goals: to address innovation needs in the electricity business sector and to ensure the security of electricity supply and resilience alongside decarbonisation efforts. The research will be performed by leading national research institutes and universities in cooperation with a highly reputed international research network and innovative user partners from the electricity business sector. The centre will provide grid companies and system operators with the methods and tools to handle the new challenges of the energy transition. SecurEL will also contribute to regulatory framework conditions that they need to meet these new challenges. The centre will develop new solutions for increasing the grid capacity at a reasonable cost, including new concepts for handling the security of electricity supply in the energy transition. A key enabler of this is comprehensive monitoring of the distribution grid, including its components and any security of electricity supply-related risks. This facilitates the use of dynamic capacity limits and improved strategies for grid operation, maintenance, and development. SecurEL will provide an important arena for exchanging knowledge, ideas, and experiences, and form the basis for these necessary joint efforts. The required interdisciplinary research in the Centre will also contribute to system innovation.

Document title: Enhancing distribution grid resilience through model predictive controller enabled prioritized load restoration strategy : preprint /
Document description: The document discusses enhancing the resilience of distribution grids through a model predictive controller enabled prioritized load restoration strategy. It proposes a priority-weighted optimal load restoration technique to improve the resilience of distribution grids against extreme events. The technique is based on smart distribution technology and framed as a sequential multistep decision process and mixed integer linear program. It is formulated as an optimal control problem with a model predictive control approach. The document presents a case study using a simplified version of the IEEE 13-bus distribution system with integrated distributed energy resources. The proposed strategy is validated in this system and demonstrates the effectiveness of the model predictive control approach in restoring the distribution grid loads based on their priority during the main grid outage-caused islanded operation. The document emphasizes the importance of quick and optimal restoration in enhancing the resilience of distribution grids and proposes an MPC-enabled prioritized load restoration strategy to improve grid resilience through the control of dispatchable distributed energy resources and seamless islanding following the incidence of extreme events.

Document title: Advanced Computing Annual Report 2021
Document description: The document discusses the National Renewable Energy Laboratory's (NREL) advanced computing capabilities and projects in the field of renewable energy. NREL researchers collaborated across disciplines to publish more than 600 technical outputs in 2021, making it the most conducted in a single year to date. The laboratory's dedicated computing facility plays a critical role in the research portfolio, and to stay at the cutting edge of high-performance computing technology, NREL finalized the contract to acquire its next-generation HPC system, named Kestrel. Kestrel will complement the laboratory's current supercomputer, Eagle, during the transition and will accelerate energy efficiency and renewable energy research at a pace and scale more than five times greater than Eagle. NREL continues to push the boundaries of efficient data center operation, with warm water cooling, optimization, and waste heat recovery enabling the facility to end the year with an average power usage effectiveness rating of 1.028. The laboratory also made advancements in scientific visualization, including the implementation of major upgrades to the Insight Center, which supports knowledge discovery in energy systems. NREL's HPC capability has supported multiple simulations using the Hierarchical Engine for Large-Scale Infrastructure Co-Simulation (HELICS) software and the Object-Oriented Controllable High-Resolution Residential Energy (OCHRE) building model. The laboratory also explored how the city of Los Angeles could achieve a 100% clean energy future by 2045, or as soon as 2035, using the Eagle supercomputer to integrate dozens of modeling tools and methods, incorporate input data from multiple sources, run more than 100 million simulations, and provide detailed results.

Document title: Sample complexity of power system state estimation using matrix completion : preprint /
Document description: This document discusses the sample complexity of power system state estimation using matrix completion. The authors propose an analytical framework to quantify the amount of data samples needed to obtain accurate state estimation in a power system. They consider the recently proposed state-estimation method for underdetermined systems using low-rank matrix completion and analyze the sample complexity of this approach. The authors incorporate constraints into the sample complexity analysis of the standard matrix completion to obtain a lower theoretical bound. They verify the significant reduction in necessary sample sizes through real-world data-based numerical evaluations using a distribution network test case. The results show that the constraints add to state estimation and can lower the number of needed samples compared to the unconstrained problem.

Document title: Sensor enabled data-driven predictive analytics for modeling and control with high penetration of DERs in distribution systems
Document description: This document presents a final scientific report on a project that aimed to develop sensor-enabled data-driven predictive analytics for modeling and control in distribution systems with high penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs). The project, which was conducted from September 2017 to February 2021, involved a team of researchers from Iowa State University and was sponsored by the U.S. Department of Energy. The report discusses the technical approach, which included the development of a combined transmission and distribution simulation model, a reduced-order model of the distribution system, and a data-driven approach for small-signal stability quantification and trajectory prediction. The report also presents the results of the project, including the impact of DERs on voltage stability margin, the effect of load unbalance on voltage stability margin, and the effectiveness of various control strategies for mitigating voltage stability issues. The report concludes that the developed models and methods can be used to improve the stability and reliability of distribution systems with high penetration of DERs.

Document title: Opportunistic hybrid communications systems for distributed PV coordination /
Document description: This document presents the results of a 3-year project on opportunistic hybrid communications systems for distributed photovoltaic (PV) coordination. The project aimed to develop a full-scale, operational implementation of the opportunistic hybrid communications systems for distributed PV coordination. The system is considered hybrid because it uses different communications pathways from the scale of residential PV inverters to a transmission network. It is opportunistic in that it chooses to route messages through each of these systems based on recent data about latency and availability to ensure reliable message passing. The project successfully developed, simulated, and validated the system, which includes the development of a communications system architecture, PV system state computation algorithms, and distributed state estimation algorithms. The system was tested and validated using various simulation models and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing. The results show that the system can effectively provide bilateral information sharing to enhance efficiency, reliability, and integrate distributed PV at large scales. Future research will focus on continuing the HIL and co-simulation validation from the perspectives of middleware, algorithms, and system-to-system.

Document description: This report details the development of HiPAS GridLAB-D, a high-performance, open-source simulation tool created to analyze electricity distribution systems for four specific California use cases: load electrification, distributed resource hosting capacity, tariff design, and system resilience. Document description: This document presents the Cooperative Research and Development Final Report on the Application of Advanced Metering Infrastructure Data to Advanced Utility System Operations. The report aims to evaluate the capabilities of Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) based controls for grid operations. The study used two SDG&E's feeders, Feeder A and Feeder B, and two AMI datasets for Feeder A. The report also developed use case scenarios, including the PV Smart Inverter Study, to examine the impact of different levels of PV penetration on feeder voltage profile using AMI data. The study found that high PV penetration levels can cause operational challenges, including voltage issues, reverse power flow, and protection issues. The report suggests that standards recommend using PV smart inverters to support the distribution grid services, specifically voltage regulation. The study evaluated the performance of each smart inverter function using multiple metrics, including the number of capacitor changes, number of LTC operations, average voltage, voltage fluctuation index, voltage unbalance index, and number of voltage exceedances nodes.

Document description: The BRIDGE initiative is a collaborative platform for European research and innovation projects in the fields of smart grids, energy storage, islands, and digitalisation. Document description: This report discusses the generation scheduling problem in hydro-dominated systems, focusing on the countries Norway and Brazil. The report reviews the main operational scheduling models and their toolchains developed and maintained by SINTEF Energy Research and the Brazilian Electric Energy Research Center. The report aims to represent the whole picture, covering some of the history of the models, and sheds light on the original ideas that motivated the creation of the models and toolchains. The report also discusses the current state of these models and how they are being developed through R&D, and the need to improve and extend the current toolchains.

Document title: Standardized Qualifying tests of electrolysers for grid services
Document description: The QualyGridS project aims to establish standardized testing protocols for electrolysers to perform electricity grid services. The project will consider alkaline and PEM electrolysers, addressing various grid services and hydrogen end users. Protocols will be applied to both alkaline and PEM electrolysers systems, using electrolyser sizes from 50 kW to 300 kW. A techno-economic analysis of business cases will be performed, covering grid and market situations in relevant European regions for large electrolysers. The project includes three electrolyser manufacturers and research institutions with experience in hydrogen technologies, electricity grid operation, and smart grids. An advisory committee will provide valuable advice, and experience from previous FCH-JU electrolyser projects and national projects will be available. The project has received funding from the Fuel Cells and Hydrogen 2 Joint Undertaking and the European Union's Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme. The project will organize workshops and symposia to exchange information with researchers and related projects, and to disseminate key lessons to relevant stakeholders.

Document title: Assessing blockchain's future in transactive energy
Document description: The electric power system is undergoing a rapid transition towards decarbonization and decentralization. Distributed energy resources (DERs) such as solar photovoltaics are threatening the traditional business model of electric utilities. Blockchain technology has been proposed as a platform to host transactive energy markets, but it is not well suited for this task due to a fundamental tradeoff between disintermediation and costs such as efficiency, scalability, certainty, reversibility, privacy, and governance. The report concludes that blockchain should not be dismissed outright, but its suitability as a platform for transactive energy markets is limited. The report makes several policy recommendations to encourage the development of transactive energy platforms that are capable of inverting the six costs. The report also assesses blockchain's suitability for other energy-relevant applications where the costs have minimal impact.

Document title: Hybrid energy systems : opportunities for coordinated research.
Document description: The U.S. power grid is undergoing transformational changes to meet the evolving demands of the 21st century. Hybrid energy systems (HES) are emerging as a key trend in the evolving U.S. energy sector, involving multiple energy generation, storage, and/or conversion technologies integrated to achieve cost savings and enhanced capabilities. HES present an opportunity to optimize power plant designs and provide various electric and nonelectric products. Recent analysis suggests advantages currently outweigh disadvantages for some technology combinations, and hybridization can help mitigate financial penalties for variable resources and overcome suboptimal technical requirements. However, challenges and uncertainties arise from the emergence of competitive HES, creating challenges for the design, operation, and regulation of wholesale electricity markets, state regulation of electric utilities, and energy policies. The U.S. Department of Energy has undertaken research and development projects to address challenges and promote innovations in HES, and the DOE Hybrids Task Force has identified opportunities for coordinated research across multiple DOE program offices.

Document title: Leveraging data portals as analytic platforms: a case study of a simulation of the Queensland Energy and Jobs Plan
Document description: This paper discusses how researchers can augment their traditional research approaches and share their large research datasets in a format easily analysed by other researchers. The case study is the Queensland Energy and Jobs Plan, and the data portal implemented using Power BI. The data portal presents the results from simulating the effect of implementing the plan on the Australian National Electricity Market, encompassing the eastern seaboard of Australia. The simulation model uses a modified version of Iowa University's open-source model of the US electricity system called Agent-based Model of Electricity Systems. The researchers used a relational database approach to capture the relationships between entities and store information about their attributes without redundancy. The paper also discusses the benefits of using relational databases within Power BI, including the ability to easily reuse large datasets from simulation modelling within the energy sector. The researchers used a hybrid machine learning and simulation approach to tackle computationally intensive simulations, and the results show that the model can provide evidence-based input into the location of new variable renewable energy and loads, and appropriate subsidies to incentivise industry to those locations.

Document description: The National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) has been a driving force in advancing wind energy technology research worldwide since its designation as a national research center in 1992. In Fiscal Year 2021, NREL continued to provide technical expertise, research capabilities, and industry understanding to support the Department of Energy's climate action and research goals. NREL received an R&D 100 Special Recognition Award for its Thermoplastic Resin System for Wind Turbine Blades, which will enable the production of recyclable blades that are stronger, longer, and less expensive. The lab also made numerous new data and modeling resources available, including a modeling tool for predicting the power performance and structural loads of wind turbines within a wind farm. NREL researchers worked on revolutionary floating offshore wind energy projects, including the Aerodynamic Turbines Lighter and Afloat with Nautical Technologies and Integrated Servo-control (ATLANTIS) program. The lab also partnered with 93 companies through 121 active agreements to advance wind energy science and lower the cost of wind-generated electricity. NREL's Microgrid Powers Campus Through Outage, and the lab's Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems (ARIES) research platform repowered the entire campus for a continuous 24 hours using 100% renewable wind and solar energy. The microgrid validated a core principle of NREL's ARIES: renewables can enhance resilience and flexibility across power systems, large and small. NREL's Eagle supercomputer helps wind energy research soar, enabling researchers to explore how complex wind dynamics affect the energy output, reliability, and cost of wind energy systems.

Document title: How can the digital transformation affect the net-zero transition?
Document description: The document explores the potential impact of the digital transformation on the transition to a net-zero greenhouse gas emissions economy. It examines the relationship between the digital transformation and the net-zero transition, focusing on energy efficiency and the carbon intensity of energy consumption. The digital transformation, driven by advances in artificial intelligence and other digital technologies, is rapidly changing production processes across different sectors in the economy. The paper presents a conceptual framework to analyse the economic mechanisms behind these green-digital transition linkages. It identifies five channels through which the digital transformation could affect the net-zero transition, including energy use of capital, capital intensity, type of energy use, direction of innovation, and scale. The overall impact of the digital transformation on the net-zero transition remains an empirical question, and the framework highlights the policy relevance of focusing on different aspects of the link between the digital transformation and the net-zero transition. The digital transformation has the potential to both accelerate and hinder the clean energy transition, and understanding its consequences for the net-zero transition is crucial to design climate policies that best account for the digitalisation of the economy.

Document description: This report by the Energy Systems Integration Group examines the potential of green hydrogen production to provide flexibility within power system models as decarbonization goals advance. The report emphasizes the challenges in modeling hydrogen, such as the need for high-resolution data, the complexity of representing different operating regimes, and the necessity of considering interactions between electricity and hydrogen markets. It calls for a shift toward best practices in modeling hydrogen flexibility, suggesting that organizations should develop initial models and continuously update them as technology and costs evolve. The text also details the data requirements for power systems, hydrogen production, and hydrogen end-use demand to accurately integrate these resources into planning studies. Ultimately, the report serves as a foundational guide for modelers to evaluate the benefits and implications of using green hydrogen to enhance system reliability and flexibility.

Document title: Trends and developments in artificial intelligence : challenges to the intellectual property rights framework : final report
Document description: This report examines the challenges posed by artificial intelligence (AI) to the intellectual property rights framework in Europe. It assesses the state of the art of AI uses in three priority domains: science, media, and pharmaceutical research. The report concludes that the current state of the art in AI does not require immediate substantive changes in copyright and patent law in Europe. However, it identifies specific avenues for future legal reform and recommends improvements in the application of existing rules. The report highlights the need to study the role of alternative IP regimes to protect AI-assisted outputs, such as trade secret protection, unfair competition, and contract law. It also notes that AI systems have become increasingly sophisticated and autonomous, but fully autonomous creation or invention by AI does not exist, and human intervention is still required in the creative process. The report focuses on the users of AI systems, rather than their developers, and examines the legal protection of AI-assisted creative and innovative outputs under EU copyright and patent laws.

Document title: The future of pumped storage hydropower
Document description: This report examines the future of pumped storage hydropower (PSH) from 2025 to 2035, highlighting its critical role in supporting variable renewable energy sources and ensuring grid flexibility. The document emphasizes that PSH is the most mature and scalable energy storage technology, capable of providing essential services like frequency stability, inertia response, and long-term energy balancing. Its long service life of over a century for civil structures and up to fifty years for equipment results in low life cycle costs and high reliability across diverse environmental conditions. By matching intermittent renewable output, PSH prevents energy waste from curtailment and replaces thermal generation, thereby contributing significantly to global decarbonization goals. The report outlines various innovative approaches including coupling PSH with hydrogen production, floating photovoltaics, and compressed air energy storage, alongside advancements in variable speed units and digital operations. It also stresses the necessity of specialized policies to reduce investment risks and proposes establishing an international standardization agency within the ISO to unify design and operational standards. The document details current technologies, construction methods, enabling technologies like digital twins and AI, and ecological considerations to provide a comprehensive roadmap for the industry's development.

Document title: Distribution Grid Operational Planning with Flexibility Resources
Document description: The document discusses the transformation of distribution grids from passive to active networks, characterized by two-way power flows and increasing flexibility. The operation of active distribution networks involves active measures, such as switching to change the grid topology, and flexibility measures, which involve the use of production and/or consumption resources, and/or energy storage. The integration of more distributed energy resources and flexibility resources has exposed major challenges, including reverse power flows, voltage issues, and increased grid losses. To address these challenges, distribution grids are transitioning toward active distribution networks, where demand is adapting to the generation available in the power system. The report proposes a comprehensive operational planning framework that enables Distribution System Operators to manage modern distribution grids efficiently. This framework addresses the need for structured long-term, mid-term, short-term, and real-time operational planning, integrating new technologies and flexibility mechanisms to ensure stability, efficiency, and resilience in evolving power networks.

Document title: An Assessment of Selected Research Programs and Goals of the Engineering Laboratory at the National Institute of Standards and Technology: Fiscal Year 2024
Document description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has engaged the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to assess the quality, effectiveness, and resource adequacy of its Engineering Laboratory (EL). The panel found that the strategies and strategic directions guiding EL's work were not clearly defined, making it difficult to assess the effectiveness of its programs. EL undertakes projects because they are feasible, rather than because they meet a clearly defined set of needs. A well-defined strategic planning process would clarify the purpose behind each program, establish clear benchmarks to measure progress, and identify go/no-go decision points. EL could consider consolidating research projects that could benefit from collaboration, improving overall efficiency. The panel also found that many research programs presented to them appeared to operate independently, with little interaction between them. This isolated approach may stem from the practice of assigning individual projects to a single principal investigator (PI), who takes sole responsibility for the project. The panel recommended that EL align its strategic planning with the needs of its stakeholders, including industry, and determine whether its work aligns with stakeholder priorities.

Document description: Brazil's power grid is highly vulnerable to climate change events, with the country ranking among the most climate-vulnerable in the world. The grid is 89% renewable, but this comes with risks, as high-impact, low-frequency events such as storms and wildfires can cause widespread outages. The country has a vulnerability score of 0.369, and in 2023, a storm in São Paulo left 2.5 million people without power. To address this, technological solutions such as grid hardening, modernization, and advanced digital platforms can be expanded, and distributed energy resources can offer local flexibility and resilience. Additionally, emergency preparedness plans and integrated planning that incorporates climate risk and biodiversity criteria are crucial. The country's resilience strategy includes a focus on biodiversity conservation, particularly the protection of the Amazon Rainforest and other critical ecosystems. Brazil's Forest Code is a comprehensive legal framework that governs the protection and sustainable use of native vegetation across Brazil. The country needs to take action to translate analytical tools and risk-assessment platforms into practical resilience measures reflected in the energy sector regulation.

Document title: Relay protection for power-electronics-dominated power grids: Technical challenges and future roadmap
Document description: The document analyzes the shift toward power-electronics-dominated grids driven by renewable energy integration and the resulting challenges for traditional relay protection systems. It explains that the low inertia and current-limiting behavior of power electronic devices cause conventional overcurrent and distance protection schemes to fail, increasing the risk of misoperation and compromising grid reliability. The report identifies significant technical challenges such as reduced fault current magnitudes and outdated standards, while simultaneously highlighting market opportunities for intelligent protection devices and new business models involving artificial intelligence and digital twins. Key technical strategies proposed include source-independent protection, adaptive distance protection using transient information, and collaborative fault identification between control and protection systems. The document emphasizes the need to adapt existing standards like IEC 61850 and develop verification standards for AI-based technologies to ensure reliability and interoperability. Finally, it outlines a roadmap for standardization and recommends policy support to foster innovation across the industrial value chain for a sustainable energy future.

Document title: Providing Ramping Service with Wind to Enhance Power System Operational Flexibility
Document description: This document discusses the challenges of maintaining power system balance with high variable and uncertain renewable resources. It presents a project that aims to develop an innovative approach to mitigate the impact of wind ramping by providing flexible ramping products from wind power. The project facilitates the efficient management of wind ramping, leading to increased dispatchability and subsequent reduction in the cost of wind integration. A probabilistic wind power ramp forecasting method was developed to characterize and forecast ramps from a utility-scale perspective. The method considers both the ramping features' dependence and wind power ramp forecasting error uncertainties. The proposed copula-based model consistently presents the closest coverage probability curve and the smallest interval score regardless of the uncertainty distribution. The project also developed an open-source Python-based market dispatch tool, OpenSMEMS, and integrated the proposed ramping product model into it. The tool was used to simulate an actual independent system operator large-scale system, demonstrating the potential economic and reliability benefits of wind providing ramping services.

Document description: This memorandum outlines the design process for the Solar+ pilot project located at the Blue Lake Rancheria Play Station 777, which integrates photovoltaic systems with battery storage and advanced controls to function as a microgrid. The project involves a collaborative team including Schatz Energy Research Center, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratories, and Serraga Energy, with distinct roles assigned to each entity for design, management, and optimization. The engineering design followed a phased approach with milestones set at 50, 90, and 100 percent completion, where detailed plans and cost estimates were reviewed by the site host at each stage. Key components include a photovoltaic array designed by McKeever Energy & Electric, a battery energy storage system by Tesla, and an islanding controller by Eaton to manage power flows and ensure safety. The electrical design incorporates a one-line diagram and network diagrams to coordinate the microgrid with the existing utility infrastructure while relegating a diesel generator to a deep backup role. Network and communications strategies were developed jointly to ensure secure data flow and cyber security compliance, supporting real-time monitoring and control of the system. The control strategy utilizes model predictive control software to optimize thermal loads and battery dispatch during both normal grid-connected and islanded operation modes. Structural considerations were made to minimize height and wind loading on the canopy while maintaining energy generation efficiency, resulting in a low tilt angle for the solar modules. The final engineering plan set includes civil, electrical, and photovoltaic sections stamped by licensed engineers to guide construction and commissioning activities.

The report also identifies ways to improve the physical resiliency of installed DERs. The report is funded by the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the U.S. Department of Energy, and it is intended to support the development of the next-generation energy sector workforce in Puerto Rico. The report provides a comprehensive set of data, models, analytic tools, and studies to support technically sound recommendations for Puerto Rico's energy investment decisions. The report highlights the need for additional engineering studies and analysis on microgrid integration and operation, as well as the need for additional guidance and requirements for DER grid support. The report also recommends some analyses and future work for the successful deployment of microgrids, especially in Puerto Rico. The report discusses the current regulations and technical requirements for integrating intentional islands in Puerto Rico, and it highlights the need for further development of regulations and technical requirements to support the deployment of microgrids.
